title: Biblical Operator Comparisons Wave 22E7

new_relations.title: Tim’s protection-and-service ethic beside Matthew 25’s least ones
new_relations.project_anchor: The project increasingly tests authority by concrete protection, nourishment, welcome and repair rather than title alone.
new_relations.biblical_structure: the judgment scene turns on feeding, welcoming, clothing, visiting and treatment of the least
new_relations.source_direction: Project ethical-fruit test first; Matthew comparison later.
new_relations.mismatch: Matthew's eschatological scene is not a generic scorecard proving any modern authority claim.
project_quote: Power is for protection. Knowledge is for understanding. Wealth is for building. Leadership is for service.
new_relations.project_context: By September 2026 Tim had compressed his mature authority ethic into a direct four-part rule: power protects, knowledge understands, wealth builds and leadership serves. In the broader Father/Gardener/King vocabulary, higher status is therefore supposed to increase concrete obligation rather than exemption.
new_relations.project_development: Matthew 25 becomes useful later because it supplies an external biblical stress test for that ethic: grand rank is not self-validating; feeding, welcome, clothing, presence and care for vulnerable people become the evidence examined in judgment.

note: Tim-side comparison upgraded to source-near wording plus context and development; Matthew remains later comparator rather than identity proof.
